plan: Deuteronomy 16:18–17:13; Deuteronomy 17:14-20; Deuteronomy 18:1-8, 9-14, 15-22; Deuteronomy 19:1-13, 14-21; Deuteronomy 20:1-20; Deuteronomy 21:1-9

readings.title: The Foundation of Justice
readings.subtitle: Appointing Judges and Officers
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 16:18] Appoint judges and officers within all your gates, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, according to your tribes, and they shall judge <dn>את</dn> the people with righteous judgment. [19] Do not distort right-ruling. Do not show partiality, nor take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous. [20] Righteousness, righteousness you shall follow, so that you live and inherit <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you. [21] Do not plant for yourself any Asherah pole near the altar of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> which you make for yourself. [22] And do not set up a pillar for yourself, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> hates.

readings.title: Maintaining Purity and Order
readings.subtitle: Judicial Procedures and the High Court
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 17:1] Do not slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> an ox or sheep which has any blemish, any evil matter, for that is an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [2] When there is found in your midst, within any of your gates which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, a man or a woman who does what is evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, in transgressing <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> covenant, [3] and has gone and served other mighty ones and bowed down to them, or to the sun or to the moon or to any of the host of the heavens, which I have not commanded, [4] and it is made known to you, and you have heard, then you shall inquire diligently. And see, if it is true and the matter is established that such an abomination has been done in Yisra’ĕl, [5] then you shall bring out <dn>את</dn> that man or <dn>את</dn> that woman who has done <dn>את</dn> this evil matter, and you shall stone to death <dn>את</dn> that man or woman with stones. [6] At the mouth of two or three witnesses shall he who is to die be put to death. He is not put to death by the mouth of one witness. [7] The hand of the witnesses shall be first against him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst. [8] When any matter arises which is too hard for you to judge, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, or between stroke and stroke – matters of strife within your gates – then you shall rise and go up to the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses, [9] and shall come to the priests, the Lĕwites, and to the judge who is in those days, and shall inquire. And they shall declare to you the word of right-ruling. [10] And you shall do according to the word which they declare to you from that place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chooses. And you shall guard to do according to all that they instruct you. [11] Do according to the Torah which they teach you, and according to the right-ruling which they say to you. Do not turn to the right or to the left from the word which they declare to you. [12] And the man who acts arrogantly, so as not to listen to the priest who stands to serve there before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, or to the judge, that man shall die. So you shall purge <dn>את</dn> the evil from Yisra’ĕl. [13] And let all the people hear and fear, and no longer act arrogantly.

readings.title: The Standards of Sovereignty
readings.subtitle: The Law of the King
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 17:14] When you come to the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, and possess it and shall dwell in it, and shall say, ‘Let me set a sovereign over me like all the nations that are around me,’ [15] you shall certainly set a sovereign over you whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall choose. Set a sovereign over you from among your brothers. You are not allowed to set a foreigner over you, who is not your brother. [16] Only, he is not to increase horses for himself, nor cause the people to return to Mitsrayim to increase horses, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has said to you, <dq>‘Do not return that way again.’</dq> [17] And he is not to increase wives for himself, lest his heart turn away, nor is he to greatly increase silver and gold for himself. [18] And it shall be, when he sits on the throne of his reign, that he shall write for himself <dn>את</dn> a copy of this Torah in a book, from the one before the priests, the Lĕwites. [19] And it shall be with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, so that he learns to fear <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> and guard <dn>את</dn> all the words of this Torah and <dn>את</dn> these laws, to do them, [20] so that his heart is not lifted up above his brothers, and so as not to turn aside from the command, to the right or to the left, so that he prolongs his days in his reign, he and his children, in the midst of Yisra’ĕl.

readings.title: The Set-Apart Portion
readings.subtitle: Provisions for the Priests and Lĕwites
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 18:1] The priests, the Lĕwites, all the tribe of Lĕwi, shall have no portion nor inheritance with Yisra’ĕl. They are to eat the offerings of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made by fire, and <dn>His</dn> inheritance. [2] And they shall have no inheritance among their brothers. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is their inheritance, as <dn>He</dn> promised them. [3] And this shall be the priest’s right from the people, from those who slaughter a slaughtering, whether it is ox or sheep: they shall give to the priest <dn>את</dn> the shoulder, and <dn>את</dn> the two cheeks, and <dn>את</dn> the stomach. [4] The first-fruits of your grain and your new wine and your oil, and the first of the fleece of your sheep, you give to him. [5] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has chosen him out of all your tribes to stand to serve in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, him and his sons forever. [6] And when a Lĕwite comes from any of your gates, from where he has sojourned among all Yisra’ĕl, and comes with all the desire of his being to the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chooses, [7] then he shall serve in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> like all his brothers the Lĕwites, who are standing there before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [8] They shall have equal portions to eat, besides what comes from the sale of his inheritance.

readings.title: A Call to Integrity
readings.subtitle: Shunning Abominations
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 18:9] When you come into the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, do not learn to do according to the abominations of those nations. [10] Let no one be found among you who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire, or one who practices divination, or a user of magic, or one who interprets omens, or a sorcerer, [11] or one who conjures spells, or a medium, or a spiritist, or one who calls up the dead. [12] For whoever does these are an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and because of these abominations <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> drives <dn>את</dn> them out from before you. [13] Be perfect before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [14] For these nations whom you are possessing do listen to users of magic and to diviners. But as for you, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has not allowed you to do so.

readings.title: The Promised Spokesman
readings.subtitle: The Prophet Like Mosheh
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 18:15] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall raise up for you a Prophet like me from your midst, from your brothers. Listen to <dn>Him</dn>, [16] according to all you asked of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in Ḥorĕḇ in the day of the assembly, saying, ‘Let me not hear again <dn>את</dn> the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, nor let me see <dn>את</dn> this great fire any more, lest I die.’ [17] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘What they have spoken is good.</dq> [18] <dq><dn>I</dn> shall raise up for them a Prophet like you out of the midst of their brothers. And <dn>I</dn> shall put <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> words in <dn>His</dn> mouth, and <dn>He</dn> shall speak to them <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>I</dn> command <dn>Him</dn>.</dq> [19] <dq>And it shall be, the man who does not listen to <dn>My</dn> words which <dn>He</dn> speaks in <dn>My</dn> Name, <dn>I</dn> require it of him.</dq> [20] <dq>But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in <dn>My</dn> Name, which <dn>I</dn> have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other mighty ones, that prophet shall die.’</dq> [21] And when you say in your heart, ‘How do we know <dn>את</dn> the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not spoken?’ – [22] when the prophet speaks in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the word does not come to be or come true, that is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him.

readings.title: Boundaries of Mercy
readings.subtitle: Cities of Refuge and Landmarks
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 19:1] When <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has cut off <dn>את</dn> the nations whose land <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, and you dispossess them and dwell in their cities and in their houses, [2] separate three cities for yourself in the midst of your land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you to possess. [3] Prepare a way for yourself, and divide into three parts <dn>את</dn> the border of your land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you to inherit, and it shall be for any manslayer to flee there. [4] And this is the matter of the manslayer who flees there and lives: when he smites <dn>את</dn> his neighbour unintentionally, not having hated him in time past, [5] as when a man goes into the forest with his neighbour to cut wood, and his hand swings the axe to cut down <dn>את</dn> the tree, and the head slips from the handle and strikes <dn>את</dn> his neighbour so that he dies, let him flee to one of these cities and live, [6] lest the revenger of blood, in the heat of his heart, pursue <dn>את</dn> the manslayer and overtake him because the way is long, and smite his being, though he was not worthy of death, since he had not hated him in time past. [7] Therefore I am commanding you, saying, ‘Separate three cities for yourself.’ [8] And if <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> enlarges <dn>את</dn> your border, as <dn>He</dn> swore to your fathers, and has given you <dn>את</dn> all the land which <dn>He</dn> promised to give to your fathers, [9] when you guard <dn>את</dn> all these commands to do them, which I am commanding you today, to love <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> and to walk in <dn>His</dn> ways all the days, then you shall add three more cities for yourself besides these three, [10] so that innocent blood is not shed in the midst of your land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you as an inheritance, and blood-guilt shall be upon you. [11] But when a man hates <dn>את</dn> his neighbour, and shall lie in wait for him and rise up against him and smite his being so that he dies, and he flees to one of these cities, [12] then the elders of his city shall send and bring <dn>את</dn> him from there, and give <dn>את</dn> him into the hand of the revenger of blood, and he shall die. [13] Your eye shall not pardon him, but you shall purge the blood of innocent blood from Yisra’ĕl, so that it might be well with you.

readings.title: The Integrity of Testimony
readings.subtitle: Witnesses and False Accusations
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 19:14] Do not move your neighbour’s boundary, which they of old have set, in your inheritance which you inherit in the land that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you to possess. [15] One witness does not rise up against a man concerning any crookedness or any sin that he commits. At the mouth of two witnesses or at the mouth of three witnesses the matter is established. [16] When a malicious witness rises up against any man to accuse him of perversion, [17] then both men who have the dispute shall stand before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, before the priests and the judges who are in those days. [18] And the judges shall inquire diligently. And see, if the witness is a false witness who has falsely accused his brother, [19] then you shall do to him as he thought to have done to his brother. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst. [20] And let the rest hear and fear, and never again do such an evil matter as this in your midst. [21] And let your eye not pardon: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

readings.title: The Conduct of Conflict
readings.subtitle: Laws of Warfare
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 20:1] When you go out to battle against your enemies, and shall see horses and chariots and people more numerous than you, do not be afraid of them, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought you up from the land of Mitsrayim, is with you. [2] And it shall be, when you draw near to the battle, that the priest shall come forward and speak to the people, [3] and shall say to them, ‘Hear, O Yisra’ĕl: You are drawing near to battle against your enemies today. Do not let your heart faint, do not fear, or tremble, or be afraid of them, [4] for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is <dn>He</dn> who goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save <dn>את</dn> you.’ [5] And the officers shall speak to the people, saying, ‘Who is the man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man dedicate it. [6] ‘And who is the man who has planted a vineyard and has not begun to use it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man begin to use it. [7] ‘And who is the man who has become engaged to a woman and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her.’ [8] And the officers shall speak further to <dn>את</dn> the people, and say, ‘Who is the man who is afraid and tender of heart? Let him go and return to his house, lest the heart of his brothers faint like <dn>את</dn> his heart.’ [9] And it shall be, when the officers have finished speaking to the people, that they shall appoint commanders of the army at the head of the people. [10] When you draw near to a city to fight against it, then you shall proclaim peace to it. [11] And it shall be, if it accepts your passage of peace and shall open to you, then all the people found in it are to be your forced labour and serve you. [12] But if it does not make peace with you, and shall fight against you, then you shall besiege it. [13] And when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> gives it into your hand, you shall smite <dn>את</dn> every male in it with the edge of the sword. [14] Only <dn>את</dn> the women, and <dn>את</dn> the little ones, and <dn>את</dn> the livestock, and <dn>את</dn> all that is in the city, all its spoil, you shall take as plunder for yourself. And you shall eat <dn>את</dn> the spoil of your enemies, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you. [15] So you do to all the cities which are very far from you, which are not of the cities of these nations. [16] But of the cities of these peoples which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you as an inheritance, you do not keep alive any that breathes, [17] but you shall certainly put them under the ban: the Ḥittite and the Amorite and the Kena’anite and the Perizzite and the Hiwwite and the Yeḇusite, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has commanded you, [18] so that they do not teach <dn>את</dn> you to do according to <dn>את</dn> all their abominations which they have done for their mighty ones, and you sin against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [19] When you besiege a city for a long time, to fight against it to take it, do not destroy <dn>את</dn> its trees by wielding an axe against them. For you do eat of them, and you do not cut them down – for is the tree of the field a man to be besieged by you? [20] Only <dn>את</dn> the trees which you know are not trees for food, you do destroy and cut down, and build siege-works against the city that is fighting against you, until it is subdued.

readings.title: Atonement for the Land
readings.subtitle: The Case of Unsolved Murder
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 21:1] When anyone is found slain on the ground which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you to possess, lying in the field, and it is not known who smote him, [2] then your elders and your judges shall go out and measure the distance to the cities which are around the slain one. [3] And it shall be, that the city nearest to the slain one, the elders of that city shall take <dn>את</dn> a heifer which has not been worked and which has not pulled in a yoke, [4] and the elders of that city shall bring <dn>את</dn> the heifer down to a wadi with flowing water, which is neither plowed nor sown, and shall break <dn>את</dn> the heifer’s neck there in the wadi. [5] And the priests, the sons of Lĕwi, shall come near, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has chosen them to serve <dn>Him</dn> and to bless in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and by their mouth every strife and every stroke is decided. [6] And all the elders of that city nearest to the slain one shall wash <dn>את</dn> their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the wadi, [7] and they shall answer and say, ‘Our hands have not shed <dn>את</dn> this blood, nor have our eyes seen it. [8] ‘O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, forgive <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, whom <dn>You</dn> have redeemed, and do not place innocent blood in the midst of <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ĕl.’ And the blood-guilt shall be pardoned them. [9] Thus you shall purge the blood of innocent blood from your midst when you do <dn>את</dn> what is right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
